neighbours.label: The slot where 'return' / 'returning' is the expected next word ('...never to return', 'when you plan on returning'): a predictor of going back
fire: The young sailor left the island in 1820, never to return.
Thousands of soldiers marched off to the front never to return home.
Let your family know which day you plan on returning from the hike.
She walked out of the village one winter morning, never to return.
Please tell the front desk what time you plan on returning to the hotel.
Her brother sailed for America and was gone, never to return to Ireland.
Before you leave, write down when you plan on returning the rental car.
The old king rode into the mountains alone, never to return.
quiet: The young sailor left the island in 1820 to hunt whales in the south.
Thousands of soldiers marched off to the front in the first week.
Let your family know which trail you will take on the hike.
She walked out of the village one winter morning to buy flour.
Please tell the front desk what time you would like breakfast.
Her brother sailed for America and found work in Boston.
Before you leave, write down the fuel level of the rental car.
The old king rode into the mountains alone to hunt deer.

predictions: The word right before an expected 'return' (never, on, to) reaches 0.4-0.8 in departure contexts; the same departure sentences continued with a purpose instead stay under 0.06.
notes: Card logit effect promotes ' recover', ' returning', ' return', ' back', ' revert'. Probe: 'travelled into that desert never to return' 0.775 (peak ' never'), 'when you plan on returning' 0.567 (peak ' on'); 'don't recover' 0.094, 'To get back to Windows' 0.032, 'never come out' 0.120; departure sentences with a purpose 0.001-0.052. Only the 'never to return' and 'plan on returning' frames scored high, so the test uses those frames.
